text:
maria: Heads-up — the quant8x4 bring-up run flagged a concentrated quality dip on very short prefixes (8–20 tokens). aggregate evals down ~12% on our 'short-answer' benchmark. seeing token collapse patterns in outputs, e.g., repeated short tokens or truncation. :thinking:
sam: Can you paste an example input + reference + model output?
maria: sure, quick one:
```
input: "What's the capital of France?"
ref: "Paris"
quant8x4_out: "Par Par Par"
```
jin: :eyes: that looks like KV-cache or attention restart problem more than pure quant noise. Did we flip any tokenizer or torch config during the build?
maria: Build had the new fused-attn kernel + the small-tokenizer patch (PR #712). I rolled kernels back and re-ran; still repros but less frequent.
nina: The tokenizer patch changed how we handle byte-pair merges for short tokens (we now normalize leading whitespace differently). Could be mapping two short tokens to same ID in edge cases. I'll diff the vocab mapping.
```
- prefix: " What's"
+ prefix: "What's"
```
sam: If tokenizer normalization maps " What's" -> "What's" that could change prefix hashes used by dedupe/holdout sampler. We might be leaking cached KV segments into unrelated requests.
labeling-bot: Re-ran golden set QA against quant8x4 on flagged short-prefix samples. 27 items flipped from ACCEPT -> REJECT. ticket: #GOLD-4567.
maria: Those 27 include a lot of templated Q/A and code-prompt snippets. Also noticed duplicates in the sample pool where near-identical short prompts exist with slight punctuation differences.
jin: We should do a two-step: 1) run a k-v cache isolation test (single-request, cold-start) to confirm.cache state; 2) resample short-prefix holdout with whitespace-normalized key so labeling matches tokenization.
sam: Agreed. For (1) can you run this quick script on staging (cold flag):
```bash
for id in $(cat short_ids.txt); do RUNTIME_COLD=1 ./run_eval --id $id --model quant8x4; done
```
maria: starting that now. ETA ~15m.
ops-bot: deploy quant8x4-a (build b233) started by @maria at 2024-04-12T14:05Z — canary on two pods.
jin: For (2) I'll create a dedupe pass that normalizes whitespace + lowercases for the sampler key. We should also surface the sampler key in the sample metadata so labelers can see why two items collided.
nina: I'll push a quick tokenizer patch that keeps previous normalization behavior behind a feature flag so we can A/B.
labeling-bot: Also scheduled a re-label batch for the 27 flipped gold items, owners assigned: @nina, @sam. deadline EOD tomorrow.
sam: If normalization fixes the dedupe mismatch, we can also run an offline regression where we re-tokenize historical prompts and diff the promptset fingerprints to estimate scale. Could be hundreds of short duplicates.
maria: result from cold-run: 18/24 repros, mostly in the templated Q/A bucket. attaching a short log snippet:
```
[run id=7] input_id=qp_234 output_tokens=[102,102,102] repeated=3 kv_state_before=0x7fffd... kv_state_after=0x7fffd...
```
jin: kv_state addresses being identical suggests kernel reused buffers incorrectly between requests when sequence len < 32. I'll repro locally with sanitizer.
nina: quick thought — if sampler dedupe is insensitive to tokenizer change, we could be training/monitoring on multiple near-duplicates which masks regressions on short prefixes. labelling + golden refresh is high priority.
sam: Plan of action: 1) isolate KV reuse bug (jin) 2) run cold-start eval on full short-prefix holdout (maria) 3) normalize sampler keys & recompute dedupe (jin) 4) re-label golden flips & expand short-prefix goldset by +200 items (nina + labeling) 5) rerun quant8x4 once kernels + tokenizer flags are addressed (sam).
maria: I'll paste a minimal repro in the thread once I have sanitizer output. thanks all. :thumbsup:
